components.summary: Framework-styled dropdown over light-DOM <option> children, opening in the top layer. filter, free, compact and multiple extend it; multiple makes it an ordered list-of-picks control.

attributes.name: value
attributes.notes: Also a live property: read `.value` for the current selection, assign it to select programmatically (no `change` fires for a programmatic set). A value matching no option shows the placeholder — unless `free` is set, which shows the raw value. With `multiple` it is the comma-separated list of picks (so value="a,b" is initial state); `.values` is the array view of the same state, readable and assignable.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.notes: Adds a filter box on top of the menu: case-insensitive match on label and value, prefix matches first, at most 100 rows rendered (a note counts the rest). Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter picks it.

attributes.name: free
attributes.notes: With `filter`: Enter commits the typed text even when it matches no option (an exact match is still picked as that option).

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.notes: Collects several values — an ordered list, not a set: `value` / `values` keep the picks in pick order, and a pill can be moved (dragged, or Alt+ArrowLeft/Right while it has focus) so an order can be built without re-picking. The picks show as removable pills in the trigger, the menu offers only what is not picked yet and stays open after a pick. `change` carries both `value` (comma-joined) and `values` (the array), including after a reorder. Pair it with `filter` for a long list.

attributes.name: min
attributes.notes: With `multiple`: the number of picks that cannot be removed (the pills' × disappears at the floor). Default 0.

attributes.name: compact
attributes.notes: Tight trigger (less padding, smaller chevron) for a crowded bar — the label gets the width back. It reflects, and sets --df-select-pad / --df-select-chev on the host; <body class="df-shell-compact"> sets the same two tokens for every select on the page.

parts.name: pill
parts.purpose: one picked value, in pick order (only with `multiple`); focusable and draggable

consumes_css_vars.affects: trigger padding (default 6px 10px; df-shell-compact and [compact] tighten it)

components.a11y: Trigger is aria-haspopup=listbox with aria-expanded (a button, or a role=combobox div with `multiple`); menu is role=listbox (aria-multiselectable with `multiple`), items role=option with aria-selected. Each pill is focusable and carries an aria-label with its position and the reorder keys; its × has an aria-label naming the value it removes.
components.example:
<druid-select name="model" placeholder="Choose model">
  <option value="a">Model A</option>
  <option value="b">Model B</option>
</druid-select>

<!-- an ordered list of values, at least one, from a long list -->
<druid-select name="langs" multiple min="1" filter value="en,de" placeholder="Languages">
  <option value="en">English</option>
  <option value="de">German</option>
</druid-select>
gotchas: Set `name` to get a hidden light-DOM input so classic form POSTs carry the value.
Options are declared as <option> children, never rendered directly; they are watched via MutationObserver.

<druid-select> is not a labelable element, so a wrapping <label> associates with nothing (label.control is null). Use a <div class="df-field"> with a <span class="df-label">, and set label="…" on the select — it becomes the trigger's aria-label.

The menu renders in the top layer (native popover, placed by druids.anchor()), so an overflow:auto or overflow:hidden ancestor — a scrolling table, a .df-dialog, a .df-card — cannot clip it. It is display:none when closed, so it never inflates the scroll height of its container. Scrolling repositions the menu rather than closing it.

Narrow hosts: the select shrinks with its container and ellipsizes the label (130px is a floor only when there is room); the menu is capped at the viewport width and ellipsizes long options, with the full text in each row's title.
Keyboard: ArrowDown opens the closed select; while open, arrows move the highlight, Enter picks it, Esc / Tab close.

`multiple` keeps its state as a comma-separated `value`, so a picked value must not contain a comma (one is replaced with a space when committed). With `name` set, one hidden input per pick is written into light DOM, all under that name — the classic multi-valued field encoding.
`multiple` renders the trigger as a role=combobox div (not a button), because the pills' × buttons cannot nest inside one; Enter or Space opens it from the keyboard.

`multiple` is ordered: a new pick is appended, and the order is the consumer's to use — a `change` after a reorder carries the same values in a new order. A pill takes focus (Alt+ArrowLeft/Right moves it, Delete/Backspace removes it, both stopping at `min`) and is draggable onto another pill's place; the order settles during the drag and one `change` fires at its end. Sort `values` yourself if the app wants a canonical order instead.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.notes: the active query; set it from the app to filter without the built-in box.

gotchas: The table is slotted light DOM: style it with .df-table and render its rows server-side as usual. The component only reorders <tr> nodes and toggles their hidden flag.
Sorting compares a cell's data-value when present, else its text; two values that both parse as numbers compare numerically. Use data-value for anything formatted ("8.1 GB", a date).
<th data-sort="none"> opts a column out of sorting (action columns).
Rows added or replaced later are picked up automatically by a MutationObserver; call refresh() only if you mutate rows in a way that does not touch the DOM.
Sticky headers and the scroll container come from .df-table / .df-table-wrap in druids.css, not from this component.

A .df-table is width:100%, so it can never outgrow the scroll container and a narrow viewport squeezes the columns. Add class "wide" to the table (or tune --df-table-min-width) to give it a width floor and get horizontal scrolling; tables with 5+ columns get that floor automatically under 720px.

The scroll container only engages if the table's ancestors can shrink: give any grid track minmax(0, ...) and any flex/grid item min-width: 0, otherwise the ancestor grows to the table's floor and the page gets the horizontal scrollbar instead. Applies to the automatic 5+-column floor too, which needs no opt-in.
